newsitem.title: UK: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.
newsitem.headline: U.K. Intervention Board details EU sugar sales.

text.p: A total 54,500 tonnes of current series white sugar received export rebates of a maximum 44.329 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at Wednesday's European Union (EU) tender, the U.K. Intervention Board said.
Out of this, traders in France received 34,500 tonnes, in the U.K. 12,500, in Spain 500, and in Denmark 7,000 tonnes, it added.
This week's award brings the cumulative tonnage awarded for export from the 1996/97 crop to 1.7345 million tonnes.
Earlier on Wednesday, London traders had expected the subsidy for the current season whites campaign for licences to end-September to be 44.329 Ecus per 100 kilos.
Traders had also forecast Wednesday's total authorised sugar tonnage export awards at between 60,000 and 65,000 tonnes versus 43,500 last week when the rebate was 44.180 Ecus.
